mergedParams.userDescription: Retro 80s chrome text with a neon glow, scan lines, and VHS wobble. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Retro 80s Chrome Text with Neon Glow & VHS Effects

prompts.prompt: Create a typokinetics preset that renders text with a full 80s chrome treatment inspired by classic arcade game titles. Think of this as building layers in After Effects - start with a base text layer, then add chrome gradients, multiple stroke layers for depth, and a neon glow composite. The text should animate in with a VHS tracking adjustment effect where the text appears to slide in from the right with horizontal RGB channel separation that settles into place. Add continuous scan lines that move vertically across the text using a repeating linear gradient, and implement a subtle VHS wobble using a sine wave transformation on the Y-axis. The chrome effect should use metallic gradients (silver to dark gray) with specular highlights that shift based on text position. The neon glow should pulse subtly, breathing life into the text like a neon sign warming up. For caption data, each word should have a staggered entrance with the chrome effect 'building up' from flat text to full chrome over 0.3s per word.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Use BaseLayout with absolute positioning containing multiple TextAtom layers for the chrome effect (base, highlight, shadow layers). Main container: 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden'. Chrome layers: Stack 3-4 TextAtom components with different z-index values, using CSS filters for metallic appearance. Scan lines: Create a separate BaseLayout with 'absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none' containing a div with repeating linear-gradient background, animated with translateY. VHS wobble: Apply a continuous transform effect with translateY using Math.sin for organic movement (amplitude: 2-3px, frequency: 2Hz). Chrome gradient: Use background-clip: text with linear-gradient(135deg, #C0C0C0, #808080, #FFFFFF, #808080). Neon glow: text-shadow with multiple layers (0 0 10px #ff00ff, 0 0 20px #ff00ff, 0 0 30px #ff00ff). Effects array: Use generic keyframe effects for opacity (0 to 1), scale (0.8 to 1), and custom filter effects for RGB channel separation. Timing: Each word from caption data gets relative timing with 0.1s stagger. Use 'ease-out' for entrance, 'linear' for continuous effects. Performance: Use will-change: transform, opacity on animated elements. GPU acceleration via transform: translateZ(0) on chrome layers.

prompts.prompt: Design a typokinetics preset as if you're creating a retro TV commercial title sequence. The text should feel like it's being displayed on an old CRT monitor with magnetic interference. Start with the text completely distorted - imagine someone holding a magnet to the screen causing the letters to warp and bend with barrel distortion. As the 'magnet' is removed, the text springs back into place with an elastic overshoot. Layer in phosphor bloom effects where bright parts of the chrome text bleed slightly, creating that characteristic CRT glow. Add horizontal hold issues where occasionally the entire text jumps up or down a few pixels, simulating sync problems. The chrome should be more subtle here - think brushed aluminum rather than mirror finish, with scan lines creating a raster effect across the surface. Include chromatic aberration that's strongest at the edges of the screen. For word-level animation, have each word 'tune in' like changing channels, with static noise transitioning to clear text.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout wrapper with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black' containing perspective container for 3D distortion. Use nested BaseLayout with transform-style: preserve-3d. Text rendering: Single TextAtom with SVG filters for distortion effects. Barrel distortion: CSS transform with perspective(300px) rotateY() for curvature, animated from 30deg to 0deg. Phosphor bloom: Use CSS filter: blur() combined with mix-blend-mode: screen on a duplicate glow layer. Scan lines: ::before pseudo-element with repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0px, rgba(255,255,255,0.03) 1px, transparent 2px). Chromatic aberration: Triple-layer TextAtom setup with red/green/blue channels offset by translateX (±2px at edges, 0px at center). Chrome effect: More subtle with background: linear-gradient(90deg, #999, #ccc, #999). Static transition: Overlay BaseLayout with animated opacity containing noise texture (CSS gradient or data URI). Effects: Generic keyframe effects for perspective transform, with spring easing for elastic bounce. Horizontal hold: Periodic translateY effect with instant transition (step easing). Timing: Use caption data for word-by-word reveal, each word taking 0.5s with 0.2s overlap. Performance: Limit blur effects to glow layer only, use transform3d() for hardware acceleration.

prompts.prompt: Build a typokinetics preset that treats text like it's part of a retro music video with heavy post-production. Imagine the text is being processed through vintage video equipment - first through a time base corrector that creates subtle horizontal warping, then through a video toaster for that characteristic 80s broadcast look. The chrome text should have an exaggerated 3D bevel effect like WordArt from the 90s, with multiple colored outlines (hot pink, electric blue, yellow) creating a print registration error effect. Add datamoshing-style compression artifacts where parts of previous frames 'stick' creating ghost trails. Implement a luma key effect where the brightest parts of the chrome occasionally 'blow out' to white with blooming. The VHS wobble should be more aggressive here, with occasional tracking errors that cause the text to split horizontally and rejoin. Sync any pulsing or glowing effects to audio beats if available, making it feel like a visualizer.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-gradient-to-b from-purple-900 to-pink-900'. Multiple TextAtom layers for 3D bevel: base, midtone, highlight, shadow (4 layers total). Registration error: Each layer offset with transform: translate(X,Y) - pink at (-2px, -2px), blue at (2px, -2px), yellow at (0, 2px). 3D bevel: Use text-shadow stacking - inner shadows for depth, outer shadows for elevation. Data-mosh trails: Use internal effect preset for motion blur, or create custom effect with multiple semi-transparent copies at previous positions. Time base corrector warp: AnimationRange effect on scaleX, oscillating between 0.98 and 1.02. Luma blow-out: CSS filter: contrast(150%) brightness(120%) with animation. VHS tracking: Occasional clip-path: polygon() animation to slice and offset text horizontally. Audio sync: If audio analysis available, use waveform effects for scale and glow intensity tied to bass frequencies. Ghost trails: Stack 3-4 semi-transparent TextAtom copies with decreasing opacity (0.3, 0.2, 0.1) and slight position offsets. Timing: Base reveal at 0.8s total, with individual character animation if not using caption data. Performance: Group transforms using CSS custom properties, use contain: layout style paint for isolation.

prompts.prompt: Conceptualize a typokinetics preset as a retro-futuristic hologram display from an 80s sci-fi film. The text should materialize like it's being drawn by a laser scanner - start with a thin horizontal line that expands vertically to reveal each character. The chrome effect here is more 'liquid metal' like T-1000, with flowing reflections that move across the surface. Add interlacing effects where every other row of pixels has reduced opacity, creating that characteristic video look. Include periodic 'signal interference' where the text briefly distorts with wave displacement, as if the hologram is losing signal stability. The neon glow should flicker occasionally like a failing fluorescent light, with moments of increased intensity followed by dimming. Implement a subtle Z-axis rotation that makes the text appear to float in 3D space. For caption-based text, have each word 'boot up' with a terminal-style cursor effect before revealing.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black overflow-hidden' plus grid overlay for hologram effect. Laser scan reveal: Use clip-path: polygon() animation from thin line to full height, or scaleY from 0 to 1 with transform-origin: center. Liquid chrome: Animate background-position on a larger gradient (200% width) for flowing effect - background-size: 200% 100%, animation: flow 3s linear infinite. Interlacing: ::after pseudo-element with repeating-linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 0px, transparent 1px, rgba(0,0,0,0.3) 1px, rgba(0,0,0,0.3) 2px). Wave displacement: Use SVG filter with feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap, animate baseFrequency value. Signal interference: Generic effect with custom filter combining blur, brightness, and hue-rotate for glitch moments. 3D float: Continuous transform: rotateY animation from -5deg to 5deg with ease-in-out. Flicker effect: Animate opacity and text-shadow intensity using steps() timing function for instant changes. Terminal cursor: ::before element with '▊' content, animated opacity for blink effect. Caption integration: Each word gets sequential reveal with 0.1s scan time per word. Performance: Use CSS containment, avoid animating properties that trigger layout recalculation.

prompts.prompt: Create a typokinetics preset inspired by retro broadcast graphics and cable TV channel identifiers. Picture the text as part of a local TV station's identity package from 1985. The chrome should be ultra-reflective with a convex curve effect, like text embossed on a metallic cylinder. Add analog video noise that creates 'snow' patterns overlaying the text, with occasional dropout where parts of the text briefly turn to static. Implement a color cycling effect where the neon glow gradually shifts through the spectrum (magenta → cyan → yellow → magenta). The VHS wobble should include head-switching noise - a horizontal band of distortion that occasionally rolls through the frame. Add film burn effects at the edges where the colors become oversaturated and blown out. For word timing, simulate a character generator typing effect where each letter appears with a slight vertical bounce, as if being stamped onto the screen.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout container with 'relative w-full h-full bg-gradient-radial from-gray-800 to-black'. Convex chrome: Use perspective transform with rotateX(10deg) for cylindrical appearance, multiple text-shadow layers for depth. Video noise: Animated BaseLayout overlay with 'absolute inset-0 mix-blend-mode-overlay opacity-20' containing noise pattern via CSS gradients. Static dropout: Random clip-path animations that temporarily hide sections, or use mask-image with gradient. Color cycle glow: CSS animation cycling through HSL values - animation: hue-rotate 4s linear infinite on filter property. Head-switch noise: Horizontal BaseLayout band with 'absolute w-full h-1' that translates vertically, containing distortion effect. Film burn: Radial gradient overlays at corners with mix-blend-mode: color-dodge, animated opacity and scale. Character generator: Each letter uses TextAtom with entrance animation - translateY from -10px to 0 with bounce easing. Chrome layers: Base metallic gradient plus specular highlight layer with animated background-position. Timing: If using caption data, map word timings; otherwise use 0.05s per character for typewriter effect. Performance: Batch DOM updates, use requestAnimationFrame for smooth noise animation if implementing via JS.

prompts.prompt: Design a typokinetics preset that mimics a retro arcade game attract screen. Think of the text as part of a coin-op machine's title screen, with excessive chrome effects and animated backgrounds. The chrome should have a multi-tier bevel with each level having different metallic tones (copper, silver, gold). Add CRT curvature to make the text appear to wrap around a curved screen surface. Implement phosphor persistence where moving text leaves brief afterimages in complementary colors. The scan lines should be more pronounced, with visible gaps between them creating a distinct raster pattern. Include a 'burn-in' effect where the text briefly appears as a ghost image offset from its main position, simulating screen burn from being displayed too long. The neon glow should strobe rapidly during entrance, then settle to a steady pulse. For dynamic text, each word should 'power up' with an electricity effect - lightning briefly connecting the letters.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black' plus barrel distortion container using CSS transforms. Multi-tier bevel: Stack 5-6 TextAtom layers with different z-index, each with unique metallic gradient - copper: linear-gradient(#B87333, #8B4513), silver: linear-gradient(#C0C0C0, #808080), gold: linear-gradient(#FFD700, #B8860B). CRT curvature: transform: perspective(400px) rotateX(5deg) scale(1.1) on wrapper. Phosphor persistence: Trail effect using 3 ghost TextAtoms with decreasing opacity and slight position lag. Raster scan lines: Dense pattern using repeating-linear-gradient with 2px transparent, 1px black lines at 50% opacity. Burn-in ghost: Duplicate TextAtom at slight offset with 'opacity-10 blur-sm' and mix-blend-mode: screen. Strobe entrance: Rapid opacity toggling using steps(2, end) timing for first 0.5s, then ease to steady pulse. Lightning effect: SVG path animation or CSS pseudo-elements with animated clip-path creating electrical arcs. Word-by-word timing: Each word from caption data gets 0.3s power-up sequence. Performance: Use transform3d for forced GPU acceleration, will-change on animated properties, contain: paint.

prompts.prompt: Build a typokinetics preset that emulates a retro video editing suite's title generator with maximum 80s excess. Imagine someone discovered every single video effect and applied them all. The text should have a chrome effect that's so reflective it shows a distorted 'environment map' - animated gradients suggesting city lights reflecting off the surface. Add a video feedback loop effect where the text appears to echo into infinity, getting smaller and more distorted with each iteration. Implement magnetic tape damage artifacts - random horizontal lines where the text becomes desaturated or shifted in hue. The VHS tracking should cause periodic horizontal tearing where the text splits and offsets before snapping back. Include a 'flying logo' effect where the text rotates in 3D space during entrance, like classic TV station identifiers. The neon glow should have multiple colors layered (pink inner, blue middle, white outer) creating a complex aura.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full perspective-1000 bg-gradient-to-br from-indigo-900 via-purple-900 to-pink-900'. Environment map chrome: Animated gradient with multiple color stops suggesting reflections - background-size: 300% 300%, complex gradient with 8+ stops. Feedback loop: Recursive TextAtom copies, each scaled down by 0.8 and offset, decreasing opacity (1, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1). Tape damage: Random BaseLayout strips with 'absolute w-full h-px' using filter: saturate(0) or hue-rotate() at random intervals. Horizontal tearing: Clip-path animation splitting text into 2-3 segments with translateX offsets, then rejoining. Flying logo entrance: 3D transform starting at rotateX(90deg) rotateY(180deg) scale(0.5) translateZ(-500px), animating to identity transform. Multi-layer glow: Stacked text-shadows - 0 0 5px #ff69b4, 0 0 10px #4169e1, 0 0 20px #ffffff, 0 0 30px #4169e1, 0 0 40px #ff69b4. 3D rotation: Continuous subtle rotateY from -10deg to 10deg for depth. Caption handling: Word-by-word reveal with 3D rotation per word. Effects array: Complex keyframe sequences for entrance, continuous wobble, and glow pulsing. Performance: Limit feedback copies to 5 max, use CSS custom properties for synchronized animations.

prompts.prompt: Create a typokinetics preset that simulates text being displayed on multiple stacked CRT monitors in a retro TV studio control room. Each word appears on a different 'monitor' with slightly different characteristics - varying levels of color adjustment, sharpness, and sync issues. The chrome effect should look like it was keyed through analog equipment, with soft edges and color bleeding. Add a vertical sync roll where the entire text occasionally scrolls vertically as if losing sync signal. Implement RGB phosphor dots visible at close range, creating a pointillistic effect. The scan lines should have interference patterns creating moiré effects when overlapping. Include analog color bars that briefly flash before text appears, and bad signal moments where text turns to colored static. The overall composition should feel like a live broadcast switching between multiple sources.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Grid BaseLayout with 'grid grid-cols-3 gap-4 p-4' for multi-monitor layout. Each 'monitor': BaseLayout with 'relative bg-gray-900 rounded-lg overflow-hidden shadow-2xl' containing text. Variable monitor effects: Each word container gets random CSS filter combinations - contrast(110%), brightness(95%), saturate(120%). Soft key edges: Use filter: blur(0.5px) on text edges, or text-shadow for softer appearance. Vertical sync roll: @keyframes roll with translateY from 0 to -100% to 100% to 0, triggered periodically. RGB phosphor dots: ::before element with radial-gradient creating dot pattern, mix-blend-mode: multiply. Moiré pattern: Multiple overlapping linear-gradients with slight angle differences creating interference. Color bars: Initial BaseLayout with striped gradient, opacity animated from 1 to 0 during entrance. Static moments: Noise overlay using turbulence filter or gradient patterns, randomly triggered. Chrome variations: Each monitor has slightly different chrome gradient parameters. Caption integration: Map each word to a 'monitor', staggered reveal timing. Performance: Use CSS Grid for layout, transform for animations, avoid layout recalculation triggers.

prompts.prompt: Design a typokinetics preset inspired by late-night retro TV commercials and used car dealership ads. The text should be aggressively chromatic with a 'rainbow chrome' effect that shifts through all spectrum colors. Add excessive star-burst effects around the text like cheesy video transitions. Implement a 'bad chroma key' effect where edges of the text have green or blue fringing as if poorly keyed. The VHS aesthetic should include severe generation loss - reduced contrast, color bleeding, and soft focus. Add random frame drops where the text briefly freezes then jumps forward. Include an 'action lines' effect with radial lines emanating from behind the text suggesting movement and energy. The neon glow should be so intense it creates lens flares and light bleeds. Make it feel like someone used every transition in their video editor's effects palette.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' containing action lines background and text layers. Rainbow chrome: Animated gradient with full spectrum - background: linear-gradient(90deg, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet), background-clip: text, animated rotation via hue-rotate. Star-burst: Multiple BaseLayout divs with 'absolute' positioning, rotated linear-gradients creating star shapes, animated rotation and scale. Bad chroma key: Green/blue outline using multiple text-shadows with color offsets - text-shadow: -2px 0 #00ff00, 2px 0 #0000ff. Generation loss: Stack filters - contrast(80%) brightness(110%) blur(0.3px) saturate(130%). Frame drops: CSS animation with steps(1) causing instant position changes simulating dropped frames. Action lines: Radial gradient background or multiple rotated divs with 'bg-gradient-to-r from-transparent via-white to-transparent'. Lens flares: Radial gradient overlays positioned at text highlights, animated opacity and scale. Text positioning: Aggressive scaling and rotation during entrance - scale from 3 to 1, rotate from 720deg. Caption timing: Rapid word reveals with overlapping timing for chaotic energy. Performance: Limit particle effects, use GPU-accelerated transforms, batch visual updates.

prompts.prompt: Build a typokinetics preset that recreates the look of retro computer graphics from 80s demo scene productions. The text should appear to be rendered on vintage hardware with limited color palettes and visible dithering patterns. The chrome effect uses a stepped gradient mimicking limited color depth - only 16 distinct gray levels creating banding effects. Add raster bars - horizontal colored bands that move vertically through the text, a classic demo effect. Implement a copper bar effect where metallic gradients cycle through the text vertically. Include screen tearing artifacts where the text occasionally splits diagonally with offset segments. The VHS wobble should be combined with low frame rate simulation - updating position only 15 times per second for chunky movement. Add a 'plasma' effect behind the text with slowly morphing color patterns. The overall aesthetic should scream 'Amiga 500 demo' with technical limitations turned into artistic style.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black' containing plasma background and text layers. Stepped chrome: Use CSS gradient with hard color stops - linear-gradient(90deg, #000 0%, #000 6.25%, #111 6.25%, #111 12.5%, ... #fff 93.75%, #fff 100%). Dithering: Overlay pattern using repeating-conic-gradient or checkered pattern at 50% opacity. Raster bars: Animated BaseLayout strips with 'absolute w-full h-4' containing gradient, translateY animation cycling through screen. Copper bars: Vertical gradient animation on text using mask-image and animated background-position. Screen tearing: SVG clipPath or CSS clip-path with diagonal splits, animated path coordinates. Low framerate: Use steps(15) timing function on position animations for choppy movement. Plasma effect: Complex radial gradients with animated positions and colors, or CSS Houdini if available. Color palette limiting: Quantize colors using calc() and CSS custom properties to nearest 16 values. Demo scene styling: Add borders, drop shadows, and grid overlays typical of era. Caption handling: Each word gets raster bar sweep on reveal. Performance: Use CSS custom properties for synchronized animations, optimize gradient calculations.
